title: Database Sharding
overview: Database sharding is a horizontal scaling technique where data is partitioned across multiple database instances (shards). Each shard holds a subset of the total data, enabling the system to handle more data and higher throughput than a single database server. Sharding is typically the last resort after optimizing queries, adding indexes, read replicas, and vertical scaling.
keyPoints: Horizontally partitions data across multiple database servers (shards)
Each shard is an independent database containing a subset of the data
A shard key determines which shard a record belongs to
Eliminates the scalability ceiling of a single database node
Cross-shard queries and transactions are complex and expensive
Rebalancing shards when adding new nodes is a major operational challenge

concepts.name: Range-Based Sharding
concepts.description: Data is divided by ranges of the shard key (e.g., user IDs 1-1M → shard 1, 1M-2M → shard 2). Simple to implement, but can create hot spots if data isn't uniformly distributed.

concepts.name: Hash-Based Sharding
concepts.description: A hash function is applied to the shard key to evenly distribute data across shards. Eliminates hot spots but makes range queries across shards impossible.

concepts.name: Directory-Based Sharding
concepts.description: A lookup table (directory) maps shard keys to shards. Flexible — shards can be added without rehashing — but the directory itself becomes a bottleneck and single point of failure.

concepts.name: Geo Sharding
concepts.description: Data is partitioned by geographic region (e.g., EU data on EU shards, US data on US shards). Reduces latency and satisfies data residency requirements.

tools.name: Vitess
tools.description: MySQL sharding middleware used by YouTube, built for massive horizontal scaling

tools.name: MongoDB
tools.description: Native sharding support with automatic chunk balancing across shards

tools.name: CockroachDB
tools.description: Distributed SQL with automatic sharding and strong consistency via Raft consensus

tools.name: Amazon DynamoDB
tools.description: Managed NoSQL with automatic partitioning; partition key is the shard key

tradeoffs: Sharding greatly improves write throughput and storage capacity but comes at the cost of increased operational complexity. Cross-shard joins become application-level operations. Distributed transactions require 2PC or saga patterns. Hot shards (uneven distribution) can undermine the performance gains. Consider sharding only after exhausting vertical scaling and read replicas.
interviewTips: Always discuss shard key selection — it's the most critical decision in sharding design
A poor shard key causes hot spots that defeat the purpose of sharding
Discuss resharding — adding a new shard requires moving data, which must be done live
Compare sharding vs. read replicas for read-heavy vs. write-heavy workloads
